How to create an OCP cluster with ROSA

Posted on 2022-04-15 | In Procedure

Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA) is a fully-managed OpenShift service, jointly managed and supported by both Red Hat and Amazon Web Services (AWS).

This article will guide you how to create and delete an OCP cluster with ROSA.

Prerequisites

  • A Red Hat account, which can access Red Hat OpenShift Console.
  • An existing AWS account, which have met the AWS prerequisites for ROSA with STS and the Required AWS service quotas. And you should obtain below access keys to use CLI utility aws, if not have then create new ones from AWS security credentials page.
    • AWS Access Key ID
    • AWS Secret Access Key
  • Enable ROSA from Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS in your AWS account
  • Get RedHat ROSA token from OpenShift Cluster Manager API Token
  • The CLI utilities aws and rosa have been installed on your laptop

Setting up the environment

Configure the AWS CLI

  • In the terminal, enter the following command:

    $ aws configure
AWS Access Key ID [None]: AKIA0000000000000000
AWS Secret Access Key [None]: eoZAW00000000000000000000000000000000000
Default region name [None]: us-east-1
Default output format [None]: json

  • Verify if the AWS CLI is installed and configured correctly

    $ aws sts get-caller-identity

Configure the ROSA CLI

  • In the terminal, enter the following command:

    $ rosa login

  • Verify if you are logged in successfully and check your credentials

    $ rosa whoami

Install and configure the latest OpenShift CLI (oc)

  • Use the rosa CLI to download the latest version of the oc CLI

    $ rosa download openshift-client

  • Extract and move the binary file to local path

    $ tar xvf openshift-client-linux.tar.gz
$ sudo mv oc /usr/local/bin/oc

  • Verify if the oc CLI is installed correctly

    $ rosa verify openshift-client
I: Verifying whether OpenShift command-line tool is available...
I: Current OpenShift Client Version: 4.10.9

Creating the ELB service role

  • Check if the AWSServiceRoleForElasticLoadBalancing role exists for your AWS account

    $ aws iam get-role --role-name "AWSServiceRoleForElasticLoadBalancing"

  • If the AWS ELB service role does not exist, create it:

    $ aws iam create-service-linked-role --aws-service-name "elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com"

Verifying AWS quota availability

  • Verify if the required resource quotas are available in your default region

    $ rosa verify quota
I: Validating AWS quota...
I: AWS quota ok. If cluster installation fails, validate actual AWS resource usage against https://docs.openshift.com/rosa/rosa_getting_started/rosa-required-aws-service-quotas.html

Creating a ROSA cluster with STS using the default options

Create the required account-wide roles and policies, including the Operator policies

  • In the terminal, enter the following command to create roles and policies:

    $ rosa create account-roles --mode auto

Create a cluster with STS using the defaults

  • In the terminal, enter the following command to create a cluster:

    $ rosa create cluster --cluster-name fusion-sds-cns --sts --mode auto -y

Track the progress of the cluster creation by watching the OpenShift installer logs

  • In the terminal, enter the following command:

     $ rosa logs install --cluster <cluster_name|cluster_id> --watch 
  
 Example:

Create users for cluster access

Creating a cluster administrator user

  • Create a cluster administrator user

    $ rosa create admin --cluster=<cluster_name>

Example:
$ rosa create admin --cluster=fusion-sds-cns
W: It is recommended to add an identity provider to login to this cluster. See 'rosa create idp --help' for more information.
I: Admin account has been added to cluster 'fusion-sds-cns'.
I: Please securely store this generated password. If you lose this password you can delete and recreate the cluster admin user.
I: To login, run the following command:
  
   oc login https://api.fusion-sds-cns.guu8.p1.openshiftapps.com:6443 --username cluster-admin --password muJet-UpYnQ-3RIer-ICCUq

I: It may take up to a minute for the account to become active.

  • Log in to the cluster through the oc CLI

     $ oc login <api_url> --username cluster-admin --password <cluster_admin_password> 

 Example:
 $ oc login https://api.fusion-sds-cns.guu8.p1.openshiftapps.com:6443 --username cluster-admin --password muJet-UpYnQ-3RIer-ICCUq

Configuring an identity provider

You can configure different identity provider types for your Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA) cluster. Supported types include GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, Google, LDAP, OpenID Connect and HTPasswd identity providers.

The following procedure configures a GitHub identity provider as an example.

  • Create a GitHub organization to use for identity provisioning for your ROSA cluster if not have. Follow the steps in the GitHub documentation.

  • Configure a GitHub identity provider for your cluster that is restricted to the members of your GitHub organization.

  • Enter the following command to set up the GitHub IdP

    $ rosa create idp --cluster=<cluster_name> --interactive

  • The above CLI will provide you with a link. Follow the URL in the output and select Register application to register a new OAuth application in your GitHub organization.

  • On the next page it will show you a “Client ID”. Copy this and paste it back into the terminal where it asks for “Client ID”.

  • The CLI now asks for a “Client Secret”. So go back in your browser and click on “Generate a new client secret” near the middle of the page towards the right.

  • Paste the secret into the terminal where the CLI is asking for the Client Secret and press enter.

  • Leave “GitHub Enterprise Hostname” blank.

  • Specify claim as the mapping method.

  • Then the IdP will be created but can take up to 1 minute for the configuration to land onto your cluster.

  • Verify that the identity provider has been configured correctly

    $ rosa list idps --cluster=<cluster_name>

Granting user access to a cluster

To configure cluster-admin privileges for an identity provider user

  • Grant the user cluster-admin privileges

    $ rosa grant user cluster-admin --user=<idp_user_name> --cluster=<cluster_name>

  • Verify if the user is listed as a member of the cluster-admins group

    $ rosa list users --cluster=<cluster_name>

To configure dedicated-admin privileges for an identity provider user

  • Grant the user dedicated-admin privileges

    $ rosa grant user dedicated-admin --user=<idp_user_name> --cluster=<cluster_name>

  • Verify if the user is listed as a member of the dedicated-admins group

    $ rosa list users --cluster=<cluster_name>

Accessing the cluster

Accessing the cluster via the Web Console

  • Obtain the console URL for your cluster

    $ rosa describe cluster -c <cluster_name> | grep Console

  • Go to the console URL in above output and use your IdP to login.

Accessing the cluster via the oc CLI

  • Log into the web console as stated above

  • Click on “Copy Login Command” in the top right corner

  • A new tab will open, Click on “Display token”.

  • You will see a login with a token command in next page like below

    oc login https://api.fusion-sds-cns.guu8.p1.openshiftapps.com:6443 --username cluster-admin --password muJet-UpYnQ-3RIer-ICCUq

  • Copy and paste it into your terminal. Press enter then can login the cluster.

  • Then you can run oc CLI commands

    $ oc get node
  
Example:
$ oc get node

Deleting a ROSA Cluster

If Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS created a VPC, you must remove network configurations(such as VPN configurations and VPC peering connections) and Any additional services that were added to the VPC firstly.

  • List your clusters in order to ensure you are deleting the correct one

     $ rosa list clusters

  • Once you know which one to delete

     $ rosa delete cluster --cluster=<cluster_name> --watch

 Example:
 $ rosa delete cluster --cluster=fusion-sds-cns --watch

  • Delete the OIDC provider that the cluster Operators use to authenticate

    $ rosa delete oidc-provider -c <cluster_id> --mode auto 

Example:
$ rosa delete oidc-provider -c 1rir0e44l46sv8lmpmhrt7uullilf1aq --mode auto
? Delete the OIDC provider 'arn:aws:iam::123926884296:oidc-provider/rh-oidc.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/1rir0e44l46sv8lmpmhrt7uullilf1aq'? Yes
I: Successfully deleted the OIDC provider arn:aws:iam::123926884296:oidc-provider/rh-oidc.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/1rir0e44l46sv8lmpmhrt7uullilf1aq

  • Delete the cluster-specific Operator IAM roles

    $ rosa delete operator-roles -c <cluster_id> --mode auto

Example:
$ rosa delete operator-roles -c 1rir0e44l46sv8lmpmhrt7uullilf1aq --mode auto
I: Fetching operator roles for the cluster: 1rir0e44l46sv8lmpmhrt7uullilf1aq
? Delete the operator roles  'fusion-sds-cns-n2l0-openshift-cloud-credential-operator-cloud-cr'? Yes
? Delete the operator roles  'fusion-sds-cns-n2l0-openshift-cloud-network-config-controller-cl'? Yes
? Delete the operator roles  'fusion-sds-cns-n2l0-openshift-cluster-csi-drivers-ebs-cloud-cred'? Yes
? Delete the operator roles  'fusion-sds-cns-n2l0-openshift-image-registry-installer-cloud-cre'? Yes
? Delete the operator roles  'fusion-sds-cns-n2l0-openshift-ingress-operator-cloud-credentials'? Yes
? Delete the operator roles  'fusion-sds-cns-n2l0-openshift-machine-api-aws-cloud-credentials'? Yes
I: Successfully deleted the operator roles

  • Use the AWS IAM Console to delete the account-wide roles which were created, such as with the prefix “ManagedOpenShift-“.

Automatic scripts

I have created scripts to auto operate above tasks, you can download them from here.
